, in order to solve the Sfm problem, it is necessary to have at least two distinct monocular images of the scene, and at least one of these images should be taken from an initial position of the camera different than the one of the other monocular image.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SfMo problem has been solved up-to-scale by using visual measurements only, but the problem is ill-posed.
the SfMM problem has been solved in the closed form, for the first time, and that the solution is very simple and intuitive.
, for the first time, the closed form solution to the SfM is provided in the case of fusing vision and inertial measurements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SfMM problem has a closed-form solution and can be solved without any prior information.
the SfMM problem is not trivial and it is not solved with a single solution, as it is usually assumed in neuroscience.
